title: Surficial geologic map of the Charleston region, Berkeley, Charleston, Colleton, Dorchester, and Georgetown Counties, South Carolina
citation: Weems, R.E., Lewis, W.C., Lemon, E.M., Chirico, P.G., and Crider, E.A., 2014, Surficial geologic map of the Charleston region, Berkeley, Charleston, Colleton, Dorchester, and Georgetown Counties, South Carolina: U.S. Geological Survey Open-File Report OF-2013-1030, map scale 1:100,000.
notes: One 1:100,000 sheet; its text layer interleaves the map face, three description columns, two cross sections and the reference list line by line. Only values whose text lies in one column on one line were recorded. Pleistocene facies descriptions (barrier-island, clayey sand and clay, fossiliferous shelf-sand, fluvial, pebbly sand facies with symbols such as Qwc, Qws, Qsbc, Qsbs, Qlc, Qtc, Qpc) could not be tied reliably to their formations and are not recorded; formations (Silver Bluff, Wando, Ten Mile Hill, Ladson, Daniel Island, Penholoway, Waccamaw(?)) are recorded by name and age only. Symbols for Holocene swamp/marsh units (Qhm, Qht, Qhsi, Qhf) not assigned. Faults: named on the cross sections, but the sections also print 'FAULTS NOT SHOWN'; recorded with the sheet's general statement that all faults are approximately located. Legend fault types (high-angle, strike-slip) not recorded. Colluvium veneer 3 to 6 ft noted as unmapped. Goddard rock-color chart reference skipped. SUBSURFACE: map face shows numerous auger hole and well points labeled with the elevation of the base of the Quaternary in feet (for example -8, -46, -77); these numbers are not tied to labels or locations in the text and are not recorded. Section distances, unit elevations and borings along A–A' and B–B' are not legible.
